Supplementary Information

This appendix accompanies the main text. Family codes identify the two-span beam (T02), no-tension bed (T04), clamped cosine strip (T08), turbine disk (T11) and shrink fit (T12). Supplementary Notes 1 and 2 give further results, controls, sensitivities and repair details; Note 3 records the selection, collection and coding protocols, and Note 4 gives the governing models and flaw certificates. Supplementary Figs. 1–6 and Tables 1–16 provide the family and harness definitions, rates and contrasts, parser and coding summaries, protocol deviations, graded quantities, model identifiers, twin controls, warning factorial and second-collection tests. The final section gives the prompt components.

Supplementary Note 1: Further results

This note holds result details that the main text summarises briefly.

Wrong solve answers.

Wrong answers in the middle of the panel are mostly recognisable (main-text Fig. 4b). Sonnet 5’s seven shortcut matches are four single-mode snap-through calculations, one Tresca face that swaps the hoop and radial stresses and two plane-strain readings of the shrink fit; Opus 4.8, Gemini 3.8 Flash and the two Sol models contribute one each. Haiku 4.5 and gpt-oss-120b mostly fail in no named way: 24 and 22 of their 25 answers fall in the residual class. Family-level counts are in Supplementary Fig. 3.

Three further checks on the confirmatory contrasts.

Three further checks bound the result. First, the 30 pairs are six draws each of five flaw designs, one per family. For both confirmatory contrasts the newer model rejects more twins in every one of the five designs (Supplementary Table 11). With five designs, no exact two-sided design-level test can fall below P=0.0625P=0.0625, so the claim is about these designs. Second, Sonnet 5 returned no usable answer on six flawed twins; excluding the pairs either model left unanswered, Sonnet 5.5 leads 19–0 over 24 pairs. Third, the older model in each version pair ran once in the first collection; the second collection (main text) repeated both contrasts.

Misses of older and smaller models.

Older and smaller models fail earlier in the same tree. Sonnet 5 runs the revealing check and concludes wrongly on 14 of 30 twins. Haiku 4.5 is unexamined on 21 of 30 and gpt-oss-120b on 16. Opus 4.8 splits across the tree: 7 rejections, 8 noted, 6 misjudged and 9 unexamined. Unlike the newer models, 5 of its 8 noted replies return numbers for the state that does not exist, such as a residual moment for a load past collapse, and 3 repair the input. Among the seven models that solve at least 22 of 25 Tier-2 items, none of the 13 Tier-2 misses is unexamined, while 25 of their 43 Tier-1 premise misses are. The flaw types differ between the tiers, so this is a description, not a test.

Supplementary Note 2: Controls, sensitivities and repair details

The main text gives each result with the numbers that carry it. This note gives the full account of each, with every count, test and caveat, in the order of the main text.

First-run rejection and planned contrasts.

Supplementary Tables 3 and 4 give the full rejection counts, false alarms and all planned contrasts. The main Results state the two confirmed version comparisons; the controls and additional estimates below delimit them. Combining the original nine pairs with the 21 added pairs gives the same direction: Opus 5 leads Opus 4.8 by 17–1 and Sonnet 5.5 leads Sonnet 5 by 25–0 (P=7.2×10−4P=7.2\times 10^{-4} and 3.6×10−73.6\times 10^{-7}; Supplementary Table 4). These pooled comparisons provide context; the confirmatory tests use only the added pairs.

Pairs whose consistent twin both models solved.

The twin allows a stricter test: rejection on the pairs whose consistent version the model solved. A model that cannot solve the consistent problem may fail the flawed one for the same reason, and the families were screened on Sonnet 5. Opus 5 solves 29 of the 30 consistent twins and rejects 22 of the matching flawed twins. Opus 4.8 solves 25 and rejects 5 of those; Sonnet 5 solves 16 and rejects 1; Sonnet 5.5 solves 28 and rejects 26 (Supplementary Table 10). Restricted to pairs that both models solved, the splits on the 21 added pairs are 13–1 for Opus 5 over Opus 4.8 (17 pairs; Holm-adjusted P=0.011P=0.011) and 9–0 for Sonnet 5.5 over Sonnet 5 (10 pairs; P=0.020P=0.020). The rejection gap is therefore not the solve gap measured a second time. This restriction is exploratory and selects pairs on an outcome. It is also weaker for the no-tension bed (T04), whose consistent twin states one graded answer (Methods; Supplementary Table 10); without T04 the splits are 12–0 over 15 pairs and 9–0 over 9 pairs (Supplementary Table 14).

Mechanical checks of the twelve noted misses.

All 12 Tier-2 misses of Fable 5.1 (3), Sonnet 5.5 (2) and Opus 5 (7) are noted. They concentrate where a stated number contradicts the model’s own calculation: 8 are the T04 gauge and 3 the T02 load past collapse. On the two flaw designs of the added pairs, a rise too small to snap (T08) and a fit that the spin test loosens (T12), these three models reject 35 of 36 twins. Two blinded coders classed every noted Tier-2 reply as a repair or a continuation (25 of 26 agreed, κ=0.92\kappa=0.92; Supplementary Table 12). In 11 of the 12, by that coding and by comparing the returned numbers with the keys, the answer belongs to an attainable reading of the statement. The eight T04 replies return the lift-off solution of the stated loads and bed, which is the key of the consistent twin, with the contradictory gauge set aside. Two of Opus 5’s T02 replies give the residual moment after unloading from the collapse state, the largest load the beam can carry, and say so in the JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) reason. Fable 5.1’s T12 reply returns zero residual pressure for a fit it calls loose. The remaining reply, Opus 5 on one T02 twin, unloads the collapse moments by the unattainable load factor; that number belongs to no state of the beam. Six of the 11 repairs are stated in the JSON reason field; five appear only in the prose.

Wall time.

Median wall time per Tier-2 solve item runs from 40 s (gpt-oss-120b) to 616 s (Sonnet 5) and does not order accuracy: Sonnet 5 solves 13 of 25, Haiku 4.5 at 433 s none and GPT-6-Astra at 223 s all 25 (main-text Fig. 6b). Wall time on subscription services includes queueing, and token counts differ in definition between harnesses (main-text Fig. 6c), so no cost ranking is claimed.

The second collection.

The confirmatory contrasts rest on one run of each older model, so a second collection, fixed before its first call and started about a day after the first collection, repeated them (Methods; main-text Table 3; Supplementary Table 16). Opus 5, Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5.5 and Sonnet 5 each received a fresh unwarned run and a schema-only run (used in the next section) on all 30 pairs, with the two arms of each model started together. A quota limit stopped 23 of Sonnet 5’s unwarned calls, so its fresh unwarned run covers 16 flawed twins, six of which ended without a reply, and the planned second unwarned runs of Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5 were not made. The Sonnet gap held. On the 10 added pairs with a final Sonnet 5 call, three of them non-answers, Sonnet 5.5 rejected 9 flawed twins that Sonnet 5 did not, and the reverse never happened (Holm-adjusted P=0.016P=0.016); counting only calls with a reply weakens this to 6–0 over 7 added pairs (Supplementary Table 16). The Opus gap did not hold. Opus 5 rejected 12 of the 30 flawed twins, against 23, 26 and 29 in its three earlier runs, and Opus 4.8 rejected 9; on the 21 added pairs the split was 2–0 (Holm-adjusted P=1P=1). Prompts, reported model identifier and command-line binary were unchanged, and Opus 5 still solved 28 of 30 consistent twins. The new replies were not coded, so whether its new misses state the flaw is not known; a word-list screen cannot decide it, because for T02 and T04 the same words occur in its replies to the consistent twins. These data cannot tell a change in the service from run-to-run variation. Opus 5’s drop from its first run, 11 flawed twins, is about two thirds of its first-run gap over Opus 4.8, 16 twins.

The warning and its two parts.

How a reply may report its status changed rejection sharply. In the first collection, a warned arm on the original nine pairs changed two things at once: it told the model to check the statement and not to solve a flawed one, and it offered a “flawed” status with a defect type in place of “cannot solve” (Supplementary Information, Prompts). On the same nine twins (main-text Fig. 5c; Supplementary Table 13), the warning raised rejection in every model that had missed any of them: Opus 5 from 3 to 9, Opus 4.8 from 1 to 9 and Sonnet 5 from 0 to 8; five models already rejected all nine. It also added false alarms in five models, up to three of nine. Counting a pair as a success only when the consistent twin is solved and the flawed twin rejected, the warning helps Opus 5 (2 to 9) and Opus 4.8 (1 to 8) and costs GPT-5.5 (7 to 4) and Gemini 3.1 Pro (7 to 6). PCBench and the trap study report the same dependence on an explicit instruction for flawed mathematical premises. The later 21 twins were run unwarned only, so the warning result rests on nine twins of three designs. Two further arms, instruction-only and schema-only, gave each part alone to five Anthropic models, about a day and a half after the unwarned and warned arms (Supplementary Table 15; Methods). Either part alone gave 43 rejections of 45 flawed twins, against 44 with both and 18 with neither in the earlier runs, with no false alarm. Because the arms ran at different times and unwarned runs vary (Opus 5 rejected 3, 6 and 9 of the same nine twins in three runs), these counts alone do not separate the causal contributions of the two parts.

The status field.

The schema-only arm of the second collection, run alongside the fresh unwarned arm, isolates the status field. Within each model, on the same pairs, it rejected more flawed twins than the unwarned arm: 18–0 for Opus 5, 21–0 for Opus 4.8 and 15–0 for Sonnet 5 (Holm-adjusted P≤1.2×10−4P\leq 1.2\times 10^{-4}), and 3–0 for Sonnet 5.5, which already rejected 27 unwarned; the three gains hold within each time window (Supplementary Table 16). On the 21 added pairs both Opus models rejected all 21 flawed twins, Sonnet 5.5 21 and Sonnet 5 18, so neither version gap passed the adjusted test (0–0 and 3–0; Holm-adjusted P=1P=1 and 0.75), although Sonnet 5 still rejected three fewer. The format also had costs. Consistent twins solved fell for Opus 4.8 (24 to 19), Sonnet 5.5 (29 to 25) and Sonnet 5 (11 to 7 of 16), and false alarms rose from none to two for Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5. Counting a pair as a success only when the consistent twin is solved and the flawed twin rejected, the schema-only arm gained for Opus 5 (12 to 30), Opus 4.8 (8 to 19) and Sonnet 5 (0 to 7) and lost one pair for Sonnet 5.5 (26 to 25). The schema lists defect types and asks for a reason, so these are effects of the whole status field, not of a single word.

Supplementary Note 3: Selection, collection and coding protocols

Selection history

Hard-10 selection uses a model-free score: shortcut failure, conditioning, and the number of regimes the item actually crosses. The top of each family, about 10% of the 1280-item pool, was frozen before any model call. That Hard-10 set has 52 solve items, 21 critique pairs and 20 premise pairs (134 items, each pair counted as two). Tier-2 families were screened on development items with Sonnet 5. A family was kept when at least two of three development items failed at the 1% tolerance and at least one failed at 5%. T02, T04, T08 and T11 were kept. T03 was dropped because Sonnet 5 solved it. T12 was developed in later calibration runs. Evaluation items are a fresh seed stream with no parameter overlap against the screening draws. New draws do not undo the model-informed choice of families: every result in this paper holds for these five families. The extension from 9 flaw pairs to 30 was designed after the original nine pairs had shown that nine could not support a pairwise claim, in order to add flaw types (T08 and T12) and to balance the original three at six pairs each. It was frozen, on its own seed stream, before any model saw those items. The Tier-2 evaluation draw was frozen with 256-bit Secure Hash Algorithm (SHA-256) manifests before any model saw it; its solve items and consistent twins are separate draws. The warned arm was not repeated on the 21 added pairs.

Run failures and excluded models

Reasoning effort was high where the command line interface (CLI) exposes the setting, and no sampling temperature or seed was set. Time limits were 1800 s on Tier 1 and 2700 s on Tier 2, where a call stopped at the limit is a failure. One Haiku 4.5 Tier-1 call exceeded the output cap twice (173 of 174 calls final). A stalled Codex connection is retried once and then graded as a harness timeout (seven GPT-5.5 calls: three solve items and four twin calls; one flawed-twin reply stalled after a rejecting status and counts as a non-rejection); an exhausted output budget, including an Antigravity call with no answer after at least 60,000 thinking tokens, is final. These non-answer rules were set or corrected during the runs (Supplementary Table 7). A call that failed in transport was retried; the first scored reply per item counts. Opus 4.6 produced no answer within 2700 s on each of 3 calls and Sonnet 4.6 recorded 23 of 61 calls, 16 at the limit; both were stopped and enter no contrast.

Single-part warning arms

Two single-part arms separate the two parts of the warning; both were fixed before their first call (Supplementary Table 7). The instruction-only arm adds the check instruction to the unwarned prompt and keeps the unwarned status options. The schema-only arm uses the warned status field and defect type without the instruction. Both ran once on the nine original pairs for Fable 5.1, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5 and Opus 4.8, with the Tier-2 settings, on 30 September, about a day and a half after the first collection; the unwarned and warned cells are these models’ first runs. The unwarned repeats of Fable 5.1, Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5 on the same nine twins give the run-to-run reference. Four exploratory contrasts on the flawed twins test the instruction with and without the warned schema and the schema with and without the instruction (exact McNemar, Holm-adjusted over the four).

Second collection protocol and interruptions

A second collection tested the two confirmatory contrasts again; it was fixed before its first call (Supplementary Table 7). Opus 5, Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5.5 and Sonnet 5 each received a fresh unwarned run and a schema-only run on all 30 pairs, flawed and consistent twin, with the Tier-2 settings. For each model the two arms started together and ran concurrently in the same item order. A subscription usage limit paused all calls for about seven hours, so collection fell into two blocks (Supplementary Table 16); every arm has calls in both blocks except Opus 4.8’s schema-only arm, which finished in the first. At the restart, 137 calls failed with a command-line sign-in error before any model reply; they were rerun. A quota guard, set to keep a share of the weekly plan free, stopped the collection after 456 of the 480 planned calls: 23 of Sonnet 5’s unwarned calls and one of its schema-only calls are missing. The planned second fresh unwarned runs of Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5 (120 calls) were not made. The prespecified tests are the two contrasts on the 21 added pairs in each arm (exact McNemar, Holm over the four), the same contrasts on all 30 pairs as combined estimates, the schema-only arm against the fresh unwarned arm within each model (Holm over the four models) and the rejection counts of every unwarned run of each model; pairs with a missing call are left out of a contrast. The new replies are scored at the status level and are not coded.

Miss-coding protocol and superseded analyses

The export lists every unwarned miss from each model’s primary run, Tier-2 and Tier-1, with a random case identifier, the problem, the planted flaw and the reply. Timeouts, budget failures and harness failures are classed automatically and are not sent to the coders. The codebook’s decision order is: an explicit statement of the contradiction is “noted”; an explicit revealing check with the wrong conclusion is “misjudged”; a reply that uses the flawed datum as given is “adopted”; a reply that never touches it is “silent”. The three-class scheme of the main text merges adopted and silent, which the coders did not apply uniformly, into “unexamined”. It was chosen after the 28 four-class disagreements were visible, so it is a post-hoc primary analysis; on the 232 cases the coders agreed with κ=0.89\kappa=0.89 on three classes and κ=0.81\kappa=0.81 on four (Supplementary Fig. 5). The coders are artificial intelligence (AI) models. Coder 1 was GPT-6-Sol through the Codex CLI at low effort. Coder 2 was Claude Sonnet 5.5 through the Claude CLI at medium effort. Both used the isolated backends. Agreed codes were kept. Each four-class disagreement was adjudicated by GPT-6-Astra through the isolated Codex CLI at high effort; it is a panel model, neither a coder nor the coding assistant, and was not involved in building or analysing the study (Use of AI tools). The adjudicator saw the codebook, four written rules, the problem, the planted flaw, the full reply and both coders’ labels, and was blind to model, run, item and the study’s aims; this arrangement was fixed before its output existed. An earlier adjudication by Claude Opus 5.5, the model behind the coding assistant, gave the same class on 26 of 28 cases and is superseded. An unblinded labelling of 42 cases by the coding assistant, made before the codebook was fixed, is not used (Supplementary Table 6).

Reason and repair coding protocol

The word lists and the repair rules above were written after the replies had been read, so both were checked by a second blinded double coding, fixed before any coder output existed (Supplementary Table 7). The export held every unwarned Tier-2 rejection of a flawed twin (289) and every Tier-2 miss coded noted (26), each with a random case identifier, the problem, the planted flaw and the full reply, and no model, run or item. A rejection reason was coded planted (the reply names the planted flaw in any wording), other defect (it claims a different defect), inability (it claims no defect and cites only the difficulty of computing) or unclear. A noted reply was coded repair (it states a corrected or attainable version and its answers fit that version), continuation (its answers are for the state the flaw makes impossible or use the flawed datum) or unclear. Coders, adjudicator, backends and effort settings were those of the miss coding. The coders agreed on all 289 reason classes (κ=1.00\kappa=1.00) and on 25 of the 26 noted replies (κ=0.92\kappa=0.92); GPT-6-Astra adjudicated the one disagreement. The coded reason class equals the word-list class for all 289 rejections, so every contrast is unchanged. For noted replies the coded class is used: it equals the rule class for 21 of the 22 replies the rules decide and assigns the four they leave as other.

Third-party solver checks

OpenSees (Open System for Earthquake Engineering Simulation), through its Python interface OpenSeesPy 3.8.0.0, repeats T02, T04 and T08 (main-text references 62, 63). T02 is a frame with zero-length elastic–perfectly plastic hinges; it checks the first-hinge factor and location, the collapse factor and the residual moment, and brackets the shakedown factor by cyclic simulation at 0.97​λs​d0.97\,\lambda_{sd} and 1.03​λs​d1.03\,\lambda_{sd}, up to 150 cycles. T04 uses compression-only springs at 5 mm spacing and checks contact length, peak reaction, largest sagging moment and end uplift. T08 uses corotational beams (main-text references 64) under displacement control, with a 10−3​h10^{-3}h antisymmetric imperfection, and checks the instability mode and critical force but not the midpoint displacement, axial force or clamp moment. Agreement tolerances are 0.1–0.2% for T02 and T04, and 3% for T08, where the keys use shallow-arch kinematics and the finite-element model does not. Flaw certificates are positive checks: for a T02 flaw, OpenSees must collapse before the stated load factor; for a T04 flaw, the gauged end must lift; for a T08 flaw, the force must rise monotonically to a stroke of twice the rise. T11 and T12 are not in this suite.

Provider harnesses and isolation

main-text Table 2 lists the panel, Supplementary Table 9 the model identifiers passed to each CLI and Supplementary Table 2 the harness settings. Anthropic models used the Claude Code CLI with an empty tool list, no project memory and no hooks; the CLI binary on the machine was dated 25 September 2026, and the version string of each call was not recorded. OpenAI GPT-6 and GPT-5 models used the Codex CLI (0.158.0) with tools, web search and user configuration disabled, in a read-only sandbox and an ephemeral session. Gemini and gpt-oss-120b used the Antigravity CLI (1.2.13), which cannot disable tools but logs every tool step. Nine Gemini 3.8 Flash calls logged a tool step; none returned a usable answer, and each is graded as a failure. No reply that used a tool is counted as correct or as a rejection. Isolation probes confirmed the Claude and Codex settings; the probe records will be released with the code after this preprint is posted.

Twin-control and reason definitions

These analyses use the existing replies and were defined after the replies had been read. They are exploratory; the analysis code and every assignment will be released with the benchmark after this preprint is posted. A pair is co-solved when both models of a contrast answer its consistent twin correctly; the contrasts are repeated on co-solved pairs. The reason of each rejection is matched against two word lists: phrases that name the planted flaw of the family (for example “gauge”, “inconsistent” and “contradict” for T04, or “burst”, “collapse” and “no equilibrium” for T11) and phrases that cite only the difficulty of computing (“without computational tools”, “by hand”, “beyond the scope”). A rejection whose reason matches only the second list is an inability rejection. Recognition of the planted flaw counts a rejection whose reason names the planted flaw, or a miss coded “noted”; a rejection that claims a different defect is not recognition.

Deterministic repair rules

Each Tier-2 miss coded “noted” is compared with the attainable readings of its flawed statement. For T04, the consistent twin shares every datum except the gauge, so its key is the lift-off solution with the gauge set aside; a reply whose answers all pass main-text equation 2 against that key is a repair. For T02, only the residual moment depends on the load factor; a residual within tolerance of unloading from the collapse state, M⁡(λc)−λc​MEM(\lambda_{c})-\lambda_{c}M^{E}, is a repair, and one within tolerance of the collapse moments unloaded by the unattainable factor, M⁡(λc)−λ1​MEM(\lambda_{c})-\lambda_{1}M^{E}, is a continuation. For T12, a reply that returns zero residual fit pressure and zero service lift-off speed treats the fit as loose and is a repair. T08 and T11 have no attainable reading of the requested state, so numbers returned for them are continuations. Anything else is “other”.

Analysis plan and additional endpoints

The analysis plan was written on 29 September 2026, after the solve items and the original nine flaw pairs had been scored and before the 21 added pairs existed. Six contrasts were named then: Opus 5.5 versus Opus 5, Opus 5 versus Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5.5 versus Sonnet 5, GPT-6-Sol versus GPT-5.6-Sol, GPT-6-Astra versus GPT-6-Sol, and Opus 5.5 versus GPT-6-Astra. Holm adjustment is applied inside each family of six. The six solve-accuracy contrasts are exploratory, because those items already existed. The six rejection contrasts are confirmatory only on the 21 added pairs; the pooled 30-pair splits are the combined estimate. All-pairs tests, 91 on solve accuracy and 91 on rejection across the 14 models, are exploratory, as are the twin controls above. The design-level statement uses an exact two-sided sign test over the five flaw designs. Four claims of the study protocol are not tested here: accuracy against cost across effort levels, the correction step of the critique arm, self-correction follow-ups and defects invisible to final-answer grading (Supplementary Table 7).

Additional scoring and collection details

The following protocol details accompany the concise Methods in the main text.

Call settings and collection details.

Main-text Table 2 lists the panel. Anthropic models used Claude Code with tools, memory and hooks disabled; OpenAI models used Codex with tools, web search and configuration disabled, in ephemeral sessions. Gemini and gpt-oss-120b used Antigravity, whose tools cannot be disabled. No reply using a tool counted as correct or as a rejection. Isolation probes checked Claude and Codex; the probe records will be released with the code after this preprint is posted. Binary identifiers, isolation settings and observed tool calls are specified in Supplementary Note 3 and Supplementary Tables 2 and 9.

Reasoning effort was high where configurable; no sampling temperature or seed was set. Time limits were 1800 s on Tier 1 and 2700 s on Tier 2. Timeouts and exhausted output budgets are failures. Transport retries, non-answer rules, incomplete models and deviations are recorded in Supplementary Note 3 and Table 7. The first scored reply counts.

The system prompt is fixed: an instruction to act as a mechanical engineer and to finish with one JSON object in a fenced block. Tier 2 appends one sentence: no tools, no code execution, no internet, calculations in the reply itself. The sentence was added after a probe returned a fabricated tool call and no answer.

Two single-part arms test the warning components: instruction-only adds the check instruction while keeping the unwarned status options; schema-only changes the status field without the check instruction. Each ran once on the original nine pairs for five Anthropic models, using Tier-2 settings. They were fixed before their first call but collected about a day and a half after the original unwarned and warned runs, so their counts alone cannot separate the components’ causal effects. The four exploratory paired contrasts and collection details are specified in Supplementary Note 3 and Supplementary Table 15.

A second collection retested the two version contrasts in fresh unwarned and schema-only arms, fixed before calls (Supplementary Table 7). Each of four models received 30 consistent/flawed pairs; its arms started together and followed the same item order over two time blocks. Quotas left 456 of 480 calls; Sonnet 5 lacks 23 unwarned calls and one schema-only call. Further older-model repeats were not made. Prespecified paired tests compare versions on the 21 added pairs, and arms within models, each Holm-adjusted over four contrasts. Missing calls are excluded; new replies are not coded. Supplementary Note 3 and Table 16 give interruptions, timings and combined estimates.

Twin-control and repair scoring details.

In T04 the consistent twin states the dial-gauge reading that the flawed twin contradicts. In five of the six T04 pairs the gauged end is the end that rises most, so the stated reading equals the graded uplift to within 0.2% and the sign of the reading shows which end lifts. The T04 consistent twin therefore states one graded answer and part of another. The co-solved contrasts are repeated without T04 (Supplementary Table 14), and Supplementary Table 10 compares the uplift answers on T04 solve items and consistent twins: older models score that answer more often on the twins than on the solve items.

A noted reply is a repair when its numbers match a physically attainable, corrected problem within main-text equation 2. Rules test the gauge-free lift-off solution (T04), elastic unloading from collapse (T02), or a loose fit (T12). Numbers for the impossible state are continuations; undecided replies are “other”. T08 and T11 have no attainable version of the requested state. Supplementary Note 3 gives the exact numerical rules.

Blinded miss-coding details.

Two blinded AI coders labelled every usable unwarned miss from the primary runs, with model, run and item identifiers hidden. Non-answers were classed automatically. The three-class scheme merges adopted and silent replies after four-class disagreements were visible, so it is exploratory. On 232 cases, agreement was κ=0.89\kappa=0.89 for three classes and 0.81 for four (Supplementary Fig. 5). GPT-6-Sol and Claude Sonnet 5.5 coded; GPT-6-Astra adjudicated blindly under a fixed protocol. No human expert validated the labels. Supplementary Note 3 retains the codebook, effort settings, adjudicator inputs and superseded analyses.

Blinded reason and repair checks.

A separately fixed blinded double coding checked the post-hoc rejection word lists and repair rules (Supplementary Table 7). It covered all 289 unwarned Tier-2 rejections and 26 noted misses, using the same coders and adjudicator. Agreement was complete for rejection reasons (κ=1.00\kappa=1.00) and 25 of 26 for repairs (κ=0.92\kappa=0.92). Word-list and coded rejection classes match throughout, leaving contrasts unchanged. Repairs use the coded class. Supplementary Note 3 defines classes, export fields and comparison with the numerical rules.

Prespecified analysis scope.

The plan was written after the solve items and original nine pairs were scored, but before the 21 added pairs existed. It named six contrasts (Supplementary Table 4), with Holm adjustment within each set. Solve contrasts are exploratory; rejection contrasts are confirmatory only on the added pairs, with 30-pair results as combined estimates. All-pairs comparisons and twin controls are exploratory. The five-design analysis uses an exact two-sided sign test. Supplementary Note 3 retains contrast definitions and planned endpoints outside this paper.

Supplementary Note 4: Governing models and flaw certificates

T02, settled two-span beam.

Hinges can form only at the five sections A, under P1P_{1}, B, under P2P_{2}, and C. Sagging moments are positive. The plastic moment at B is the smaller of the two span values. Elastic response at load factor λ\lambda, with settlement Δ\Delta at B, is the force-method compatibility condition

𝐅​𝐗+λ​𝜹P+𝜹Δ=𝟎,\mathbf{F}\,\mathbf{X}+\lambda\,\boldsymbol{\delta}_{P}+\boldsymbol{\delta}_{\Delta}=\mathbf{0}, (S1)

and M⁡(x)=M0​(x,λ)+∑jXj​mj​(x)M(x)=M_{0}(x;\lambda)+\sum_{j}X_{j}m_{j}(x). The first-hinge factor λy\lambda_{y} is the smallest λ\lambda at which |M||M| reaches MpM_{p} at a hinge section. Collapse is the minimum, over mechanisms, of internal plastic work over external work. Shakedown uses Melan’s theorem: λs​d\lambda_{sd} is the largest factor for which a residual moment field keeps λ​ME+ρ\lambda M^{E}+\rho inside the plastic moments for every load path in the domain (main-text references 48, 49, 50). Reference A uses Koiter’s kinematic dual (main-text references 51); reference B uses linear programming of the static form. The residual moment after loading to λ1\lambda_{1} and elastic unloading is M⁡(λ1)−λ1​MEM(\lambda_{1})-\lambda_{1}M^{E}. The flawed twin sets λ1>λc\lambda_{1}>\lambda_{c}.

T04, compression-only bed.

E​I​w′′′′+k​w​H​(w)=∑iPi​δ​(x−xi),k=ks​b,EI\,w^{\prime\prime\prime\prime}+k\,w\,H(w)=\sum_{i}P_{i}\,\delta(x-x_{i}),\qquad k=k_{s}b, (S2)

with HH the Heaviside function. In the Winkler reaction k​wkw, k=ks​bk=k_{s}b is the foundation modulus of a bed of width bb (main-text references 47). The compression-only switch, the bed pushing only where the deflection is downward, is the unilateral contact of Weitsman and of Tsai and Westmann (main-text references 52, 53). The contact interval is unknown. Lifted parts carry zero moment and shear and stay straight. The sign conditions are the optimality conditions of the convex potential Π(w)=12∫EIw′′2+12∫k⟨w⟩2−∑iPiw(xi)\Pi(w)=\tfrac{1}{2}\int EI\,w^{\prime\prime 2}+\tfrac{1}{2}\int k\,\langle w\rangle^{2}-\sum_{i}P_{i}w(x_{i}), with ⟨w⟩=max⁡(w,0)\langle w\rangle=\max(w,0). Two minimisers can differ only by a rigid-body motion a+b​xa+bx, and such a motion changes the bed energy wherever the beam is in contact. Equilibrium under the downward loads requires a contact zone of positive length, so the contact solution is unique. The flawed twin places a downward gauge reading at an end the other data lift off the bed.

T08, clamped cosine strip.

Both ends are clamped. As in the shallow-arch theory of Fung and Kaplan (main-text references 54), axial compression NN is the integral of the change in squared slope, and the transverse equilibrium is

E​I​(y−y0)′′′′+N​y′′=−P​δ​(x−L/2),EI\,(y-y_{0})^{\prime\prime\prime\prime}+N\,y^{\prime\prime}=-P\,\delta(x-L/2), (S3)

with the clamped cosine shape y0=(h/2)​(1−cos⁡2​π​x/L)y_{0}=(h/2)(1-\cos 2\pi x/L) of Qiu, Lang and Slocum (main-text references 55). The strip loses stability at the earlier of a force maximum on the symmetric path and the asymmetric bifurcation N=N2N=N_{2}; low arches show this competition between symmetric and asymmetric modes (main-text references 54), and a clamped buckled beam switches to the asymmetric mode when the axial load reaches N2N_{2} (main-text references 56). Reference A expands the deflection in the symmetric buckling modes (2000 modes kept) (main-text references 57). Reference B uses Hermite finite elements under midpoint displacement control. The flawed twin sets h/th/t between 0.75 and 1.0. On that range the symmetric path has no force maximum and N<0.9​N2N<0.9\,N_{2} throughout, so the strip the prompt calls a snap-through switch never loses stability.

T11, spinning disk.

Plane stress, free bore, rim tension from the blades proportional to ω2\omega^{2}. The elastic field is the standard rotating-disk solution (main-text references 35). In the plastic zone a≤r≤ca\leq r\leq c the Tresca face is σθ−σz=Y\sigma_{\theta}-\sigma_{z}=Y with σθ≥σr≥0\sigma_{\theta}\geq\sigma_{r}\geq 0, and radial equilibrium integrates to

r​σr=Y⁡(r−a)−ρ​ω23​(r3−a3).r\,\sigma_{r}=Y\,(r-a)-\frac{\rho\omega^{2}}{3}\bigl(r^{3}-a^{3}\bigr). (S4)

The associated flow rule gives zero plastic radial strain, so the radial displacement in the plastic zone follows from σr\sigma_{r} and YY alone (main-text references 58, 59). For a solid disk, Gamer showed that the textbook Tresca solution violates the associated flow rule (main-text references 60). For the annular disk with a free bore used here we keep the face σθ−σz=Y\sigma_{\theta}-\sigma_{z}=Y with σθ≥σr≥0\sigma_{\theta}\geq\sigma_{r}\geq 0, and every accepted instance certifies that the plastic hoop strain is non-negative and grows with speed. The face σθ−σr=Y\sigma_{\theta}-\sigma_{r}=Y is a shortcut that gate R5 catches. Unloading is elastic. Residual stress and permanent bore growth are the elastic–plastic state minus the elastic solution at the same overspeed. The flawed twin sets the overspeed above the burst speed.

T12, shrink-fitted disk.

The fit pressure falls linearly with ω2\omega^{2} until lift-off. Above lift-off the disk is a free-bore T11 disk. After the overspeed the residual interference is the installed interference minus the permanent bore growth, and the service lift-off speed scales with the square root of the residual pressure (main-text references 61). Certificates required at build time: the fit opens before any yielding, and re-contact is elastic. The flawed twin states that the fit stays tight, with the interference set to 0.70–0.85 of the permanent bore growth, so the disk is loose.

Supplementary figures

Supplementary tables

An item random-intercept logistic model on the solve items was fitted by maximum a posteriori estimation, the marginal likelihood taken by non-adaptive 30-point Gauss–Hermite quadrature, with a normal prior of mean 0 and standard deviation 2.5 on the model effects. The item-difficulty standard deviation is 0.79 on the logit scale. Model effects (logit, standard error) run from +3.89+3.89 (1.16) for Opus 5 and GPT-6-Astra, through +0.03+0.03 (0.45) for Sonnet 5, to −3.98-3.98 (1.16) for Haiku 4.5 and gpt-oss-120b. The fit converged. It is a description of the spread, not a ranking test.
